name: Innovation in Government Initiative (J-PAL): policy partnerships (Founders Pledge)
summary: J-PAL's Innovation in Government Initiative (formerly the Government Partnership Initiative) funds partnerships that help governments adopt evidence-backed policies. Founders Pledge's 2019 estimate values two reforms it helped bring forward: India's fund-flow reform of its rural employment scheme, and Zambia's scale-up of Teaching at the Right Level.

rows.label: Annual salary increase per SD
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: Founders Pledge's 2023 figure, 19.1% a year per standard deviation of learning (facts: founders_pledge_2023.salary_increase_per_sd). Its 2019 method, which this analysis used, assumed 10% (kept in the evaluator view). Founders Pledge's own models of education rest on two methods: its 2019 one (earnings +10% per standard deviation of test scores, 80% of it additional, lasting 5 years, no household) and its 2023 one (+19.1% per standard deviation, times 17.5% for replicability, lasting a 40-year working life, doubled for the household). Our view uses Founders Pledge's latest for every education model, so a standard deviation of learning is worth the same wherever it comes from.

rows.label: Share of the increase that counts
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: Founders Pledge's 2023 method counts 17.5% of the measured earnings gain, its replicability adjustment for the evidence linking test scores to earnings (facts: founders_pledge_2023.replicability_adjustment). Its 2019 method counted 80% as additional (kept in the evaluator view). Founders Pledge's own models of education rest on two methods: its 2019 one (earnings +10% per standard deviation of test scores, 80% of it additional, lasting 5 years, no household) and its 2023 one (+19.1% per standard deviation, times 17.5% for replicability, lasting a 40-year working life, doubled for the household). Our view uses Founders Pledge's latest for every education model, so a standard deviation of learning is worth the same wherever it comes from.

rows.label: Spending on Teaching at the Right Level per child (our estimate)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Government Partnership Initiative CEA (evidence-based policy report, 2019)

rows.explainer: Ours, not Founders Pledge's: needed for the correction below. FP's 0.02 SD per dollar for Teaching at the Right Level, against an effect of about 0.15 SD per child (the TaRL evidence FP's education sheet uses), implies about $7.50 per child. The range is ours: $5 to $15, covering cheaper government-run delivery and costlier first years of a scale-up.

rows.label: Present value of ln(income) per student
rows.explainer: Corrected (changed for consistency). FP's sheet multiplies the gain in test scores per dollar (0.0138 SD per $) by the number of children, as if it were a gain per child; its own figure is 0.00345 ln(income) per student. We multiply by the dollars spent per child first, so the gain is per child. The evaluator view keeps FP's number, so its sheet still reproduces.

source.title: Founders Pledge, Government Partnership Initiative CEA (evidence-based policy report, 2019)

rows.explainer: Median result in GiveWell's 2017 cost-effectiveness analysis (version 5), in the same unit.

rows.label: Times as cost-effective as GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line: the cost per child-life equivalent of GiveDirectly over the initiative's, both in GiveWell's 2017 units. Comparing in multiples of cash mostly cancels how those units value a child's life, though India's freed-up money is valued in them directly.

rows.label: Units of value per child-life equivalent
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. A child-life equivalent is GiveWell's 2017 unit of value: Founders Pledge values India's freed-up money in it (governments' cost of an outcome as good as saving a child's life, $13,615 to $16,774), and GiveWell's 2017 moral weights fix what it is worth against income (GiveDirectly at $11,663 per child-life equivalent, so 39 units of value at the shared cash benchmark). The site values every death averted with one shared figure, so a child-life equivalent counts as what it says, an under-five death averted: GiveWell's current moral weight, 116.25 units of value, times the weight on a life under Your values. The evaluator view keeps 39.07 (11,663 × 0.00335), which reproduces Founders Pledge's multiple of cash.

rows.label: Units of value per unit of ln(income)
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. Founders Pledge turns Zambia's income gain into child-life equivalents with GiveWell's November 2016 moral weights (a unit of ln(income) is 1/3 of a DALY, a child's life 7 DALYs), so a unit of ln(income) is 1/21 of a child-life equivalent: 1.86 units of value, read against GiveDirectly. The site values every gain in ln(income) the same way, for every model: the weight on income under Your values (1 / ln 2 = 1.44 at the default, one doubled income-year = 1 unit of value). The evaluator view uses Founders Pledge's 1.86, which reproduces its multiple of cash.

rows.label: Benefit of the Zambia reform at the site's weight on income (child-life equivalents)
rows.explainer: The present value of Zambia's income gain, times the years the reform was brought forward, valued at the site's weight on income and put in child-life equivalents so it can be added to India's (the value of a child-life equivalent cancels for Zambia). Founders Pledge's 7 DALYs per child life and 3 units of ln(income) per DALY drop out; in the evaluator view this equals Founders Pledge's own figure.

rows.label: Both reforms re-valued, relative to Founders Pledge's total
rows.explainer: India's child-life equivalents as Founders Pledge counts them, plus Zambia's at the site's weight on income, over Founders Pledge's total. 1 in the evaluator view.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's multiple of cash divided back by GiveDirectly's $11,663 per child-life equivalent is the initiative's child-life equivalents per dollar (so GiveWell's 2017 GiveDirectly figure cancels), with Zambia re-valued at the site's weight on income, each worth the site's value of an under-five death. In the evaluator view this is Founders Pledge's multiple of cash times the shared cash benchmark.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Your value, shared with every model built on an organisation's past average (Your values: "How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far"): Founders Pledge divides the Initiative's budget to date by the two reforms it helped bring forward, an average; the next dollar does less than the average dollar did, since an organisation pursues its best opportunities first. 50% by default (our judgment), from 18% to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row above).
